findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The operator was unable to provide food handler certificates for any of the employees who are not CFPMs. Popeye’s is not on the Illinois Approved Food Handler Training List and therefore, must require all employees to have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. Due to this violation being a third repeat violation, this violation is now on compliance conference. A follow up is scheduled on 4/3/2026 to ensure that all employees who are not CFPMs have obtained their food handler certificate, or according to Colleen Kelley, the Director of Environmental Health, the permit for the facility will be suspended. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The operator was unable to provide food handler certificates for any of the employees who are not CFPMs. Popeye’s is not on the Illinois Approved Food Handler Training List and therefore, must require all employees to have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. It is recommended to reach out to the Illinois Department of Public Health to be placed on this list if the onboarding training qualifies. Ensure that this process is taken or that all employees have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) Upon entering the facility, there was not a present CFM. CFM arrived after a phone call to return from running an errand. The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11  (C) Employee observed drinking from an uncovered cup. See violation #16 as well. Discussed appropriate beverage containers during the inspection.  Employee observed drinking from an uncovered cup in the food preparation area. Provide a lid and straw for beverage cups. Reference 2-401.11.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Multiple employees observed improperly washing hands. Staff is observed properly washing hands and then touching faucet with clean hands and dispensing paper toweling with clean hands before drying. In-order to eliminate cross-contamination, dispense paper towel prior to washing hands and use towel to turn off contaminated faucet.  Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 0 ppm at frontline sani-bucket. Buckets are present from previous night. Closing staff should make facility ready for next day's operations. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11  (P) Observed employee using his personal cup as a scoop within the ice bin. The lip of the cup was in contact with employee's mouth prior to scooping ice. Discussed cross-contamination with staff.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) In-Use utensils are observed being stored in a non-operating dipping well. The water was just turned off due to flooding of the floor. Water was again flowing during the inspection.   Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12 (D) =  in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, if used with moist food such as ice cream or mashed potatoes;

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) and (C)  (C)  Grease and soil accumulation is observed on the interior vents of the top of the prep cooler. Thoroughly clean all cooking equipment and pans. Reference 4-601.11(B) and (C).
